title: OpenAI splits Daybreak into Blue and Red tiers and ships GPT-5.6-Cyber, its first 'offense-grade' security model
subtitle: Daybreak Blue drops production-side prompt filters for vetted defenders on GPT-5.6 Sol, and Daybreak Red opens a purpose-trained cybersecurity model to a partner network that includes IBM, CrowdStrike, Cisco, Accenture and Cloudflare.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program on August 10 into two access tiers and released a new model, GPT-5.6-Cyber, purpose-trained on offensive and defensive security work. Daybreak Blue runs GPT-5.6 Sol with production-side security-content filters lifted for vulnerability discovery, secure code review, malware analysis and incident response. Daybreak Red goes further — vetted partners get GPT-5.6-Cyber for vulnerability research, exploit validation and adversarial testing. The launch partner roster includes IBM, CrowdStrike, Accenture, Cisco and Cloudflare.

OpenAI's headline benchmark is stark: GPT-5.6-Cyber answered 95.0% of prompts on its internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate test, versus 2.0% for GPT-5.6 Sol behind Blue's relaxed filters and 1.5% for stock Sol. The gap is what OpenAI is calling 'offense-grade' — a model that will actually answer questions about writing an exploit rather than politely declining. That is exactly the capability defensive teams have been complaining they don't have access to, and exactly the capability that regulators and safety researchers have spent two years arguing shouldn't be widely released.

The two-tier design is the compromise. Access is gated: Blue requires an enterprise agreement and identity attestation, Red requires that plus a partner-program review, and neither is available to the general public. Consumption is metered, prompts are logged, and OpenAI retains the right to revoke a partner's access. It is a very deliberate mirror of Microsoft's MAI-Cyber-1-Flash rollout on August 3, which routes exclusively through Azure AI Foundry, and of Google's July release of Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber for restricted government use — three of the four biggest labs are now shipping cyber-specialized models the same quarter, all through pay-per-use gated channels.

For learners: the safety debate around frontier cyber models is not going to be settled by whether the capability exists — it clearly does — but by who gets to hold the key. Study the access controls, not just the benchmarks. Ask who can sign into Daybreak Red, how quickly access can be revoked, what OpenAI sees in the request logs, and what a partner is legally allowed to build on top. Those answers describe the actual risk surface. The model card is a small part of the story; the contract, the audit log and the revocation path are most of it.
